extracted.intended_audience: women (wives and mothers) seeking practical guidance on creating and maintaining a happy home
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive guidance for wives and mothers on building and preserving a happy household through manners, money management, patience, and small domestic practices. The advice addresses interpersonal dynamics between spouses and household routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order, Kindness and Mutual Forbearance
rubrics_metrics.description: The general principles underlying home-making are roughly Order, Kindness and Mutual Forbearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three are likened to the beams, uprights and roofing of a household; they underlie everything that enters into the comfort and pleasure of the household, collectively and individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home is made by Presence, not by House
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the house that makes the home ... It is the Presence, the nameless influence which is the earliest acknowledged by the child, and the latest to be forgotten by man or woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furnishings and architecture alone do not create a home; the woman's sustaining presence and personal influence transform rooms into 'our rooms' and create the welcoming atmosphere at the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to the small sub-laws / 'chink-fillers' (little things matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chats will deal with certain sub-laws often overlooked so that 'the wind finds its way through chinks'; little things that are trifles can let discomfort into a home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: leaving a bit of fancy work with needle and scissors, placing a favorite chair or song at twilight, small personal touches on tables and lamps—these trivial-seeming acts fill the chinks and make the home intimate and welcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Woman's prerogative and responsibility in establishing the Home
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of this power is essentially woman's prerogative; without feminine agency no house, however well appointed, can be anything higher than an official residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The wife/mother as representative of sympathy and love provides the moral and emotional atmosphere of the home; her labor and influence are central to preserving the 'seedtime' of character in children and the domestic sanctuary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness and Conventionalities ('Gospel of Conventionalities')
rubrics_metrics.description: Small civilities and conventional courtesies (lifting one's hat, rising when she enters, courteous table and drawing-room behavior) are essential to domestic harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Politeness elevates the wife in her own and others' eyes, encourages neatness and becomingness in dress, and are peaceable fruits that prevent 'checking' (cracks) in domestic relations. Politeness must be home-made rather than purchased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have realistic expectations about male nature and difference
rubrics_metrics.description: John is not and never can be a woman; wives should not expect exact sympathy of taste, opinion, and feeling from their husbands simply because they are married.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize differing standpoints and upbringing; failure to accept these differences and to expect men to mirror women is an 'irrational longing' that breeds disappointment. Measure husbands by appropriate (masculine) standards rather than feminine ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage husband's foibles with tact—coaxing rather than direct confrontation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many husbands 'need, in double harness, to be cleverly managed, to be coaxed and petted up to what else would make him shy; if driven straight at it, the chances are ... he will balk or bolt.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical techniques: 'plough around stumps' rather than force, time matters (wait until he has dined), insinuate schemes so he feels they are his own, use gentle persuasion and humor rather than blunt argument to carry plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve the husband's dignity; keep his faults private
rubrics_metrics.description: While John remains loyal, 'the inventory of his faults should be a sealed book to her closest confidante; the carping discussion of his failings be prohibited by pride, affection and right taste.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion and reticence are virtues; airing a husband's shortcomings undermines marriage and violates good taste. Forbearance and gratitude are recommended over public criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual understanding over the Family Purse (ownership of family income)
rubrics_metrics.description: The crying need of a mutual understanding with respect to the right ownership of the family income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial arrangements should be negotiated to avoid heart-burnings, contentions and secret unhappiness; historical practices of enforced dependence caused hardship. Examples like paying married daughters a weekly share illustrate one approach; the chapter signals the need for clear agreements about money within marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home-cooked food and personal care create sentiment and attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Men often prefer home-cooked fare because there is individuality in the steak broiled for 'John' and sentiment in pains taken to sweeten a dish with love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic food, prepared with personal attention and served with a smile, acts as a message from the heart and fosters return and attachment; the familiarity and personal touches of home fare are not replaceable by hotel cookery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate forbearance and charity; accept quarrels as surface-gusts
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasional clash of opinions or passing heat of temper are surface-gusts that do not stir the brooding love of hearts at rest in one another; given fidelity and devotion, wives should show forbearance with offensive peculiarities and lack of appreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain perspective; marriage is more than momentary disagreements. The author urges gratitude for devotion and recommends restraint from overblown criticism to preserve the deeper bonds.
